info.desc: Artistically and commercially, the Stevie Nicks/Lindsey Buckingham/Mick Fleetwood/Christine and John McVie edition of Fleetwood Mac had been on a roll for over a decade when Tango in the Night was released in early 1987. This would, unfortunately, be Buckingham's last album with the pop/rock supergroup -- and he definitely ended his association with the band on a creative high note. Serving as the album's main producer, Buckingham gives an edgy quality to everything from the haunting "Isn't It Midnight" to the poetic "Seven Wonders" to the dreamy "Everywhere." Though Buckingham doesn't over-produce, his thoughtful use of synthesizers is a major .

podcast.body: Christine McVie was the biggest hitmaker from this Fleetwood Mac album. The album included her song "Everywhere," which cracked the Top 30 on the Hot 100 in January 1988 and became one of the band's most acclaimed hits. "It made McVeigh the biggest hitmaker from Fleetwood Mac's Tango in the Night Album, not the first LP where that had occurred."

podcast.body: Initially conceived as Lindsey Buckingham's third solo album, Mick Fleetwood persuaded him to transform it into the next Fleetwood Mac album. Buckingham took full producer credit for the first time on a Mac album, and its creation took 18 months, longer than "Tusk," a process Buckingham later called "the worst recording experience of his life." He compiled songs from fragments contributed by other members, including Mick Fleetwood and Stevie Nicks, both battling cocaine addiction at the time. "The resulting LP, Tango in the Night, was in essence a Lindsey Buckingham album disguised as Fleetwood Mac."
